body:
# Independent audit: full-rank sampled volume and deficient sampled mass

Audited source:
`candidate 631839b23c1a0508`.


constant is exact and sharp. The multi-level conclusion is conditional
on its stated level count, volume ratio, and lower-rank OC hypotheses;
the case with one fine integer coordinate uses only ordinary Grunbaum.

## 1. A triangulation using every actual sampled point

The sampled set P is finite because the source is compact and the
lattice is discrete. Its convex hull is full dimensional under the
rank hypothesis. A triangulation of a convex polytope using only its
extreme vertices exists, for example by a pulling triangulation.

For an additional point p, there is a unique face F of the current
simplicial complex whose relative interior contains p. Stellar
subdivision at F replaces its entire star, including every incident
full simplex. For each incident simplex, join p to the facets that
do not contain F. The subdivisions agree on common faces. This
works when F lies on the boundary as well as in the interior, and
retains every previous vertex. The complex remains a pure
r-dimensional triangulation; hence each newly inserted point is
a vertex of at least one full-dimensional simplex. Iterating over
the finite set P proves exactly the existence assertion needed.

For a simplex in a lattice coset, subtracting one vertex removes
the coset offset. Express its r edge vectors in a lattice basis.
Their determinant is a nonzero integer. Thus its Euclidean volume
is at least v/r!, with no orthogonality assumption on the lattice.

## 2. Fiber volumes and the exact Dirichlet coefficient

All vertex fibers are nonempty compact convex sets. Their s-volumes
may vanish. Brunn--Minkowski remains valid for these degenerate sets,
and convexity gives the Minkowski inclusion in the actual fiber.
For integer s>=1,

    (sum_i alpha_i b_i^(1/s))^s >= sum_i alpha_i^s b_i.

When a coefficient or b_i is zero, its term is simply zero. No
division by a vanishing fiber volume occurs. On an r-simplex Delta,

    integral_Delta alpha_i^s
       = |Delta| r! s!/(r+s)!.

The factor r! in this expression is essential and is present in the
source. Combining it with |Delta|>=v/r! gives v s!/(r+s)! for every
vertex incidence. Summing over disjoint simplex interiors is valid
by Fubini; section-volume functions are measurable. Every vertex is
counted at least once. The integral over conv(P) is at most the
full volume of Q, so no equality Q=conv(sampled source) is required.

Consequently the displayed inequality

    M >= v s!/(r+s)! T

holds including boundary-only sampled fibers. If T>0 and P has full
rank, the right side is positive, also proving full ambient volume.

## 3. Sharpness, including approximation by all-positive fibers

Here is an additional exact calibration of the constant. Work first
with the standard lattice, and take the unimodular base simplex
Delta=conv(0,e_1,...,e_r). These are its only lattice points. Put an
s-dimensional convex body K of volume one at base zero and the
singleton {0} at every other vertex. Let Q be their convex hull.
For barycentric coordinates alpha, its fiber is exactly alpha_0 K.
Therefore

    T=1,
    M=integral_Delta alpha_0^s=s!/(r+s)!.

This Q is full dimensional in R^(r+s). Applying a base lattice
basis map gives equality for arbitrary covolume v.

If all sampled fibers are required to have positive s-volume,
replace the other vertex fibers by epsilon K, epsilon>0. The fiber
at alpha is (alpha_0+epsilon sum_(i>0)alpha_i) K. Writing
h_s(a_0,...,a_r)=sum_(|beta|=s) product_i a_i^(beta_i), direct
multinomial integration gives

    M/v = [s!/(r+s)!] h_s(1,epsilon,...,epsilon),
    T=1+r epsilon^s.

Their ratio tends to s!/(r+s)! as epsilon decreases to zero. Thus
strict positivity of every sampled fiber does not permit a larger
uniform constant either.

## 4. Lower-rank levels and exact measure preservation

For a deficient level with positive sampled mass, choose lambda_0
in its sampled set. The span V of differences is rational relative
to L, so V intersect L is a rank-r' saturated sublattice. Moreover

    (lambda_0+V) intersect (L+a)
       =lambda_0+(V intersect L).

A lattice basis identifies this coset exactly with Z^(r'). The
source can first be replaced by the hull of all its sampled fibers:
this is contained in Q and contains each entire sampled fiber, so
all original sampled fibers are unchanged and no new sampled base
is created. Its base projection is conv(P), and lattice convexity
of P follows from convexity of the original projection.

Positive sampled s-volume supplies the full vertical R^s direction.
Together with the r'-dimensional base span, this proves that the
hull is a full convex body in its reduced R^(r') times R^s space.
The lattice basis map changes only base coordinates. In particular
its potentially nonunit r'-Jacobian does NOT enter the fiberwise
H_s measure or the normalized mixed depth.

Every original closed halfspace containing the selected point has
a restriction to this reduced affine hull which is a containing
closed halfspace or the whole hull. An empty restriction is
impossible. Thus a lower-rank depth guarantee contributes exactly
its own unnormalized mass to every original cap. No limiting
irrational plane or approximate center is used.

## 5. Mass accounting and the conditional target

Let c=(r+s)!/s! and eta=M/(vT). Summation over only the full-rank
levels gives T_full<=cM/v. Hence deficient levels carry at least
(1-c eta)_+ of total sampled mass. With at most J sampled levels,
some deficient level has at least that fraction divided by J.
Assuming OC for ranks at most r-1, its deterministic center gives

    depth_original >= [(1-c eta)_+/J] 2^(-(r-1)) Gamma_s.

When eta<=1/(2c) and J<=2^k this is at least
2^(-k-r) Gamma_s, exactly as stated. Equality in the assumptions
causes no strictness loss. Coarse levels without fine samples may
be included in M and only make the volume-ratio assumption stronger.
Sampled levels carrying zero H_s mass may be counted in J and only
weaken the averaging bound. If r=1 every deficient positive level
has r'=0, so ordinary continuous Grunbaum is the only depth theorem
used, for every s>=1.

For s=0, the claimed volume formula would already fail for an
interval of length Nh with N+1 lattice sample points. The source
correctly excludes this case rather than using a zero-root limit.

The independent verifier `supporting computation verify_sampled_projection_volume_audit.py`
checks the Dirichlet/multinomial coefficients, the sharp simplex
family, and the conditional depth factors by exact rational
arithmetic. It is an arithmetic cross-check; the triangulation and
lattice reduction proofs above supply the geometric justification.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
